claims.feature: other: the record that does not survive
claims.claim: Wolfe says none of his Plant Engineering magazine articles have been reprinted anywhere.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, written reply to Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013
claims.quote: none of my magazine articles have been reprinted anywhere

claims.claim: Ultan's Library dates Wolfe's Plant Engineering employment 1972 to 1984.
claims.source: Nigel Price, 'Gene Wolfe's time at Plant Engineering', Ultan's Library, 2013

claims.claim: Plant Engineering's own obituary of Wolfe dates his senior editorship 1972 to 1986, four years later than the terminal date Ultan's Library gives.
claims.quote: senior editor of Plant Engineering magazine from 1972 to 1986

claims.claim: Wolfe says being the Letters to the Editor editor at Plant Engineering was good and fun and taught him a lot of stuff.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: which was good and fun and taught me a lot

claims.claim: Asked to name the best editors he had worked with, Wolfe named David Hartwell first and called him his principal editor.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: He's been my principal editor over the years

claims.claim: Wolfe placed Damon Knight second among the editors he had worked with, after Hartwell.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Lawrence Person, 'Suns New, Long, and Short', Nova Express Vol 5 No 1, Fall/Winter 1998 (blog reprint 2021)
claims.quote: Damon Knight would have to come in second

claims.claim: Dirda reports that every one of Wolfe's stories and novels goes through at least three drafts and occasionally as many as ten.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: at least three drafts, occasionally as many as 10

claims.claim: Dirda reports that at Plant Engineering Wolfe bought some twenty-five free-lanced articles a year.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: buys some 25 free-lanced articles a year

claims.claim: Dirda reports that Wolfe wrote a major cover story for Plant Engineering every few months while writing The Book of the New Sun.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: writes a major cover story every few months

claims.claim: Wolfe says he is never sure he is through with a manuscript until he mails it out.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Michael Dirda, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: Until I mail a manuscript out I'm never sure

claims.feature: other: what an editor made of him
claims.claim: Wolfe says his dedication of The Fifth Head of Cerberus to Damon Knight commemorates Knight growing him from a bean.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Michael Dirda, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: when he grew me from a bean

claims.feature: other: what an editor made of him
claims.claim: Dirda describes Damon Knight as a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, reporting, The Washington Post Book World, 30 January 1983
claims.quote: a mentor to many contemporary science fiction writers

claims.feature: other: an editor changing the form not the sentences
claims.claim: Wolfe says Damon Knight liked 'Trip, Trap' but not its double-column format, and asked him to break it into conventional alternating sections.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: Knight liked the story but not its double-column format
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'

claims.feature: other: an editor marking the cut points
claims.claim: Wolfe says Knight returned the story marked to show the points at which he felt the switches from one letter to the other should be made.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: marked to show the points at which he felt
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'

claims.feature: other: an editor marking the cut points
claims.claim: Wolfe says he spent a couple of hours trying to improve on Knight's marked switch points and found he could not.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Contemporary Authors Autobiography Series Vol. 9, quoted on WolfeWiki
claims.quote: I spent a couple of hours trying to improve
claims.page: 'A note about the writing of the story'
